title: What a Member's Liability on a Line Put Right is Worked Out From
content:
Where a line under one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders is put right, the amount the member's liability is worked out from is settled by the network standing of the provider who gave the line and by how what the provider charged stands against the allowed amount.

## The rule

**Where the line put right was given by a provider outside the network**, the member's liability is worked out from what the provider charged, a provider outside the network not being held to the allowed amount.

**Where the line put right was given by a provider inside the network and what the provider charged is above the allowed amount the line carries**, the member's liability is worked out from the allowed amount the line carries, a network provider not being permitted to bill the member above it.

**Otherwise**, the member's liability is worked out from the lower of what the provider charged and the allowed amount the line carries.

## Condition and amount

| Network standing | What the provider charged, against the allowed amount | The amount the liability is worked out from |
|---|---|---|
| Outside the network | Any | What the provider charged |
| Inside the network | Above the allowed amount | The allowed amount |
| Inside the network | At or below the allowed amount | The lower of the two, that is what the provider charged |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

Take a line put right carrying an allowed amount of 700.00 USD.

- **Outside the network, the provider having charged 950.00 USD:** the liability is worked out from 950.00 USD.
- **Outside the network, the provider having charged 600.00 USD:** the liability is worked out from 600.00 USD.
- **Inside the network, the provider having charged 950.00 USD:** the liability is worked out from 700.00 USD, the network provider not being permitted to bill above the allowed amount.
- **Inside the network, the provider having charged 600.00 USD:** the liability is worked out from 600.00 USD, the lower of the two.
- **Inside the network, the provider having charged 700.00 USD:** what was charged is not above the allowed amount, and the liability is worked out from 700.00 USD.

The fourth and fifth cases sit on either side of nothing: what matters in the third case is only whether what the provider charged stands above the allowed amount.
